title: Bootloader sprintlet: 45min SDK playbook (sketch)
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, timeboxed playbook for a 45-minute internal 'sprintlet' to get an engineer from zero to a working Redwood SDK integration (local dev + smoke tests + minimal telemetry). The goal is not a production rollout but a reproducible, instrumented prototype that exposes the most common friction points and gives clear next-step artifacts for a follow-up sprint.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: backend/mobile/web engineers who need to embed Redwood inference calls into an app or microservice.
- Scope: onboarding package + smoke scenarios + telemetry probes + triage checklist. Not covering enterprise onprem installs or Dedicated capacity negotiation.

Outcomes (45m):
1) Local dev app makes a sample generation call to Redwood hosted API (success + streaming).
2) Basic instrumentation: request/latency/cost tagged and sent to dev telemetry (local mock or minimal backend).
3) Smoke test harness runs 3 scenarios (short prompt, long-conversation warmup, embedding lookup).
4) Short write-up of two clear blockers (if any) and one optimization candidate to hand to runtime team.

Prereqs (before sprintlet):
- Participant has Git + Node or Python installed.
- Redwood API key in env var: REDWOOD_API_KEY.
- Minimal sandbox project scaffold fetched: git clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdks-sprintlet-starter.git
- (Optional) Local proxy for replay: http://localhost:8080

Timebox (45m):
- 0–5m: Kickoff & alignment (owner quickly verifies env and repo).
- 5–18m: Quick install + auth check + hello-world generation call.
- 18–30m: Add streaming + fallback test, run smoke flows.
- 30–38m: Add minimal telemetry (latency + token cost) and wire to local endpoint.
- 38–43m: Run smoke harness, capture logs, create issue(s).
- 43–45m: Closeout: saved artifacts, next-step assignment.

Quick step-by-step (Node example):
1) Install: npm ci (in starter dir)
2) Export key: export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_live_xxx
3) Run auth check (script included): node scripts/auth-check.js
   - Expected: 200 + model list JSON (if failure, capture request id).
4) Hello gen: node examples/hello-gen.js
   - Example snippet in file:
     const Redwood = require('@redwood-inference/sdk');
     const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
     const res = await client.generate({ model: 'redwood-alpha-1', prompt: 'Write a 2-sentence marketing blurb for a note app' });
     console.log(res.text);
5) Streaming test: node examples/stream-demo.js (use --simulate-loss to test reconnection)
6) Embedding smoke: node examples/embed-check.js (checks vector length and cosine sanity)

Minimal telemetry (15 lines to ship):
- Capture: request_id, model, route, tokens_in, tokens_out, latency_ms, status_code.
- Where to send: default to local endpoint POST http://localhost:5001/telemetry or stdout if missing.
- Format: JSON lines, one per request. Keep schema tiny.
- In code: wrap client's request call with timer + token counter helper.

Smoke harness (3 scenarios):
- S1 short prompt (latency < 200ms median on hosted region)
- S2 long conversation: 5-turn warmup then generation (verify kv cache warmpath)
- S3 embedding: embed 5 strings, check deterministic length and basic neighbors.

Failure modes to highlight quickly:
- Auth errors: invalid key (401) — common cause: stale env or copy/paste error. Action: run auth-check and attach redwood-request-id.
- Network: streaming stalls — simulate with --simulate-loss. Validate retry/backoff in client.
- Latency spikes: check route/model mismatch (e.g., sending long prompt to low-latency small-token profile). Flag to runtime team with sample prompt and logs.

Acceptance criteria for this sprintlet:
- Hello-gen returns valid text for S1 and log contains telemetry line for request.
- Streaming demo emits at least one chunk and final delta.
- Embedding script returns numeric vectors and similarity matrix prints without exceptions.
- One GH issue created if any unexpected friction; else update README with notes.

Artifacts to produce by closeout:
- PR: README augmentation with quick start commands and what failed (if anything).
- GH issue linking to logs and redwood-request-ids (label: sdk-sprintlet).
- Short feedback note in Confluence page (link above) with a tag: "sprintlet-complete".

Ops notes / handoff template (copy into GH issue):
- Repro steps (commands run)
- Environment (OS, Node/Python version, region inferred)
- Logs (attach telemetry lines)
- Observation: latency/cost anomaly or API contract ambiguity.

Lightweight checklist for workshop leads:
- [ ] Confirm each participant has API key and can run auth-check.
- [ ] Provide spare keys in a central repo if someone is blocked.
- [ ] Ensure telemetry endpoint is reachable and accepts JSON lines.
- [ ] Capture 3 redwood-request-ids per participant for debugging.

Notes to self (rough):
- Consider adding a tiny local mock server to simulate Dedicated fallback; useful for diagnosing routing policy issues quickly.
- Try a one-button GH Actions job that runs the smoke harness and posts result to PR. Low friction for non-technical reviewers.
- Need an abridged legal blurb for external partners re: API key usage during workshops.

Open questions (for follow up sprint):
- Should the starter scaffold include automatic telemetry upload to console (opt-in)?
- What minimal telemetry retention is safe for internal demos (PII concerns)?
- Feasibility of shipping the starter as both Node and Swift Playgrounds for mobile engineers.

Related links and quick refs:
- Confluence notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=987654
- Starter repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdks-sprintlet-starter
- GH PR for telemetry adapter: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-bootloader/pull/42
- Example ticket: JIRA ENG-2217

End of sketch.

(Loose-format doc: intentionally short, with TODOs inline; this is meant to be iterated in a working session.)
